assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Emission
items.clue: The giving out of radiation by an object.

items.label: Peak wavelength
items.clue: The wavelength at which a body emits most intensely.

items.label: Wavelength distribution
items.clue: How the emitted radiation is spread across a range of wavelengths.

items.label: Perfect black body
items.clue: An object that absorbs all of the radiation incident on it, reflecting none of it and transmitting none of it.

options.text: All objects do, whatever their temperature happens to be
Only objects hot enough to glow red, orange or white
Only objects that are warmer than the air near them
Only objects that have a dull, matt black surface

questions.explanation: All bodies (objects), no matter what temperature, emit and absorb infrared radiation.

questions.stem: An ice cube at −15 °C is put on a plate in a warm room. Which statement about the ice cube is correct?

options.text: It absorbs radiation but is much too cold to emit
It emits radiation, but it absorbs more than it emits
It only absorbs, because the room around it is warm
It emits no radiation until it warms up to 0 °C

questions.explanation: All bodies emit radiation; the cube is colder than the room, so absorption outweighs emission.

questions.stem: Two identical iron blocks are held at 30 °C and at 80 °C in the same room. Which statement about the infrared radiation they emit is correct?

options.text: Neither block emits until it is hotter than the room air
The 80 °C block emits more radiation in a given time
Both emit equally, since the blocks are identical
Only the 80 °C block emits any radiation at all

questions.explanation: The hotter the body, the more infrared radiation it radiates in a given time.

questions.stem: A lamp filament is heated from dull red to bright white. How does the radiation it emits change?

options.text: Only the intensity rises; the wavelength range is unchanged
Only the peak shifts; the intensity stays the same
The intensity rises and the peak moves to shorter waves
The intensity rises and the peak moves to longer waves

questions.explanation: Both the intensity and the wavelength distribution of the emission depend on the temperature of the body.

questions.stem: What happens to radiation that is incident on a perfect black body?

options.text: Most is absorbed, but a small part is reflected
It is all absorbed and stays trapped in the body
All of the radiation is absorbed by the body
Some is absorbed, the rest passes through

questions.explanation: A perfect black body absorbs all of the radiation incident on it, reflecting and transmitting none.

questions.stem: Two stars are the same size. Star A looks blue-white and star B looks red. What can be concluded?

options.text: Star B is hotter, since red light carries more energy
Star A is cooler, as blue light has a shorter wavelength
They are equally hot but made of different gases
Star A is hotter, and its peak wavelength is shorter

questions.explanation: The wavelength distribution depends on temperature: the hotter star peaks at shorter wavelengths.

questions.stem: A perfect black body would be the best possible emitter of radiation. Why?

options.text: It stores the radiation it absorbs and lets it out later
Its surface is black, and black surfaces look hottest
It reflects and transmits only a tiny amount
A good absorber of radiation is also a good emitter

questions.explanation: Since a good absorber is also a good emitter, a perfect black body would be the best possible emitter.

questions.stem: (HT only) A metal plate inside a hot oven has reached a constant temperature. What does this tell you about the radiation?

options.text: It absorbs radiation as fast as it emits it
It has stopped absorbing and emitting any radiation
It still absorbs radiation but no longer emits any
No radiation is absorbed or emitted now

questions.explanation: A body at constant temperature is absorbing radiation at the same rate as it is emitting radiation.

questions.stem: (HT only) The temperature of a body is rising. Which statement must be true?

options.text: It absorbs and emits radiation at the same rate
It is absorbing radiation and emitting none at all
It is absorbing radiation faster than it emits radiation
It is absorbing radiation, and emission cannot cool it

questions.explanation: The temperature of a body increases when the body absorbs radiation faster than it emits radiation.

questions.stem: (HT only) Which factors does the temperature of the Earth depend on?

options.text: Only how close the Earth sits to the Sun in space
Only the distance of the Earth from the Sun and its orbit
Only how much radiation the Earth takes in from the Sun
The rates of absorption and emission, and reflection to space

questions.explanation: The temperature of the Earth depends on many factors including the rates of absorption and emission of radiation and reflection of radiation into space.

questions.stem: (HT only) The ground cools quickly on a clear night, but much less on a cloudy night. Why?

options.text: Cloud radiates energy back down, so the net loss is smaller
Cloud acts as an insulating layer, stopping conduction of heat
Cloud completely stops the ground emitting radiation upwards
Without cloud, the warm air is not trapped near the ground

questions.explanation: The ground still emits, but it now absorbs radiation from the cloud as well, so the imbalance is smaller.

questions.stem: (HT only) An energy-balance diagram shows short-wavelength radiation arriving from the Sun and long-wavelength radiation leaving the Earth's surface. Why is the outgoing radiation longer in wavelength?

options.text: The radiation loses energy as it travels up through the air
The surface of the Earth is far cooler than the Sun
The atmosphere stretches the waves as they pass through
Only long waves can escape into space from the ground

questions.explanation: The wavelength distribution depends on the temperature of the body, and the surface is far cooler than the Sun.
